A rectangular block of clay is being reshaped as it moves through a press. Its height is decreasing at a rate of $0.5\,\text{ft/min},$ its width is increasing at a rate of $1\,\text{ ft/min},$ and its length is decreasing at a rate of $2\,\text{ft/min}.$ How fast is its volume changing when its dimensions are $10\,\text{ft}$ in length, $4\,\text{ft}$ in width, and $3\,\text{ft}$ in height? Assume that the rate of decrease of volume is positive.

The volume of the rectangular block of clay is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
${\text{ft}}^{3}\text{/min}.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $L,$ $W,$ $H$ and $V$ be the length, the width, the height, and the volume of the box, respectively. We know that

$$
\begin{aligned}L=10\text{ ft},\, & W=4\text{ ft}, \\ H=3\text{ ft},\, & \frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}t}=-2\text{ ft/min}, \\ \frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t}=1\text{ ft/min},\, & \frac{\text{d}H}{\text{d}t}=-0.5\text{ ft/min}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}.$

The relation between the four variables is given by the formula for the volume of a rectangular prism:

$$
V=LWH
$$

We differentiate both sides of $V=LWH$ with respect to $t,$ using the product rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}V & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(LWH) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =W\cdot H(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}t})+L\cdot H(\frac{\text{d}W}{\text{d}t})+L\cdot W(\frac{\text{d}H}{\text{d}t}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can plug in the known values and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =(4)(3)(-2)+(10)(3)(1)+(10)(4)(-0.5) \\  & =-14{\text{ ft}}^{3}/\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the rectangular block of clay is decreasing at a rate of $14{\text{ ft}}^{3}/\text{min}.$
